source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Viewing the family as interdependent members, so that a change in one member affects the whole family, reflects which framework?
questions.rationale: Systems theory sees the family as an interrelated, interdependent unit; a change in one part changes the whole.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Theoretical perspectives (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: a change in any one part inevitably results in changes in the entire system.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse anticipates that a couple with a newborn must adjust to accepting a new member. She is applying which framework?
questions.rationale: The developmental approach views the family through its life cycle and predicts stage-related demands.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Theoretical perspectives (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: in the life cycle stage of families with young children, the key principle of emotional process of transition is accepting new members into the family system

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is the first family health task?
options: Recognize the health condition or problem
Provide nursing care to sick members
questions.rationale: The five tasks: recognize, decide on action, provide care, maintain a healthful home environment, use community resources.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Family health tasks (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: (1) recognize the presence of a wellness state or health condition or problem

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: First-level assessment in family nursing ends with the identification of:
questions.rationale: First-level assessment identifies wellness states, health threats, health deficits and stress points; second-level identifies family nursing problems.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Nursing assessment (PDF p. 55)
questions.quote: specific health conditions or problems are identified and categorized as: (1) wellness state/s; (2) health threats; (3) health deficits; and (4) stress points

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: "Inability to provide nursing care to the bedridden grandfather due to lack of knowledge of the procedure" is a statement derived from:
questions.rationale: Second-level assessment states the family's inability to perform a health task and the reason (etiology).
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Steps in family nursing assessment (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: The family nursing problem is stated as an inability to perform a specific health task and the reasons (etiology) why the family cannot perform such task.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A family keeps rat poison on the kitchen table within reach of a toddler. In the typology, this is a:
questions.rationale: Health threats are conditions conducive to disease or accident, e.g., improperly kept poisons and medicines.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 69)
questions.quote: pointed/sharp objects, poisons, and medicines improperly kept

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A family member has untreated pulmonary tuberculosis. In the typology of family nursing problems, this is a:
questions.rationale: Health deficits are instances of failure in health maintenance: illness states, failure to thrive, disability.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 70)
questions.quote: Presence of Health Deficits — instances of failure in health maintenance.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: For the other members of the family with a TB patient, the risk of catching the disease is classified as a:
questions.rationale: Threat of cross-infection from a communicable disease case is a health threat.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 69)
questions.quote: Threat of cross infection from a communicable disease case

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A family's eldest child is starting school next month. This is classified as a:
questions.rationale: Stress points are anticipated periods of unusual demand: marriage, pregnancy, entry to school, adolescence, job loss, death.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Entrance at school

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A 2-year-old who is not gaining weight according to normal rates represents a:
questions.rationale: Failure to thrive/develop according to normal rates is a health deficit.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 70)
questions.quote: Failure to thrive/develop according to normal rates

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A couple knows their son has a lump but refuses to have it checked because they fear it is cancer. Their nursing problem is inability to recognize the problem due to:
options: Denial from fear of the diagnosis
questions.rationale: Under the first health task, denial about the problem's existence or severity due to fear of consequences is a listed cause.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Denial about its existence or severity as a result of fear of consequences of diagnosis of problem

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A mother cannot decide whether to bring her sick child to the health center because her husband and mother-in-law disagree. This falls under inability to:
questions.rationale: Conflicting opinions among family members about action to take is a reason under the decision-making health task.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Conflicting opinions among family members/significant others regarding action to take

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A family stopped going to the health center after a health worker scolded them. Their problem is failure to utilize community resources due to:
questions.rationale: A previous unpleasant experience with health workers is a listed reason under the fifth health task.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Typology (PDF p. 73)
questions.quote: Previous unpleasant experience with health worker

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which tool graphically displays family members and their relationships across three or more generations?
questions.rationale: A genogram shows generational structure and relationships; an ecomap shows the family's ties with outside systems.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Data-gathering tools (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: Genograms graphically display information about family members and their relationships over at least three

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: To see how a family relates with the school, church, health center and relatives outside the home, the nurse uses a(n):
questions.rationale: An ecomap diagrams the family's relationships with the external environment and its resources.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Data-gathering tools (PDF p. 63)
questions.quote: An ecomap visually diagrams the family? s interactions or relationships with the external environment and its resources.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: During a home visit, the nurse sees that the family's water container is uncovered and the toilet is unsanitary. The data-gathering method used is:
questions.rationale: Observation uses the senses to gather data on the home, interactions and conditions.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 2 Data-gathering methods (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: This method of data collection is done through the use of the sensory capacities-sight, hearing, smell and touch.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In the scale for ranking family health problems, which criterion carries the heaviest weight (2)?
questions.rationale: Weights: nature 1, modifiability 2, preventive potential 1, salience 1; total 5.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Scale for ranking (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: The highest score is 5, equivalent to the total weight.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: "The probability of success in improving or eliminating the problem through intervention" defines which priority-setting criterion?
questions.rationale: Modifiability is the probability of success in enhancing wellness or minimizing the problem through intervention.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Prioritizing (PDF p. 78)
questions.quote: Modifiability ofthe condition or problem - refers to the probability ofsuccess in enhancing the wellness state, improving the condition

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The family's own perception of how serious and urgent a problem is refers to:
questions.rationale: Salience is the family's perception and evaluation of the problem's seriousness and urgency; felt needs raise the score.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Prioritizing (PDF p. 78)
questions.quote: Salience - refers to the family's perception and evaluation of the condition or problem in terms of seriousness and urgency of attention needed

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In priority setting, which type of condition receives the lowest score under "nature of the problem"?
questions.rationale: Wellness states and health deficits get the highest score; foreseeable crisis the least, as Filipino families usually have support to cope.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Factors affecting priority-setting (PDF p. 80)
questions.quote: Foreseeable crisis is given the least weight because culture- linked variables/ factors usually provide our families with adequate support

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A problem is "partially modifiable" (score 1 out of a highest of 2; weight 2). Its computed score for modifiability is:
questions.rationale: (Score ÷ highest score) × weight = (1 ÷ 2) × 2 = 1.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Scoring (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: Divide the score by the highest possible score and multiply by the weight: (Score / Highest Score) x Weight

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which factor increases the preventive potential of a health problem?
questions.rationale: Exposure of high-risk groups and appropriate current management raise preventive potential; severity and long duration lower it.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Factors affecting priority-setting (PDF p. 80)
questions.quote: Exposure of any vulnerable or high-risk group increases the preventivepotential of a condition or problem.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A cardinal principle in setting goals of family nursing care is that goals must be:
questions.rationale: Joint goal setting ensures the family's commitment to achieving the goals.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Goals and objectives (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: A cardinal principle in goal setting states that goals Inust be set jointly with the family.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A rural family without a toilet does not see open defecation as a problem. This barrier to joint goal setting is:
questions.rationale: Often only the nurse sees the problem while the family is satisfied, e.g., improper waste disposal.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Goals and objectives (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: Failure on the part of the taniily to perceive the existence of the problem.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which type of nurse-family contact gives the best chance to observe the actual care given by family members in their environment?
questions.rationale: The home visit is costly in time and effort but best for appraising relationships, the home and family competencies.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Nurse-family contact (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: the best opportunity to observe actual care given by family members

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An advantage of the clinic conference over the home visit is that it:
options: Lets the nurse use clinic equipment
questions.rationale: Clinic conferences are less expensive, allow use of equipment and other team members, and promote family self-responsibility.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Nurse-family contact (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: The clinic or office conference is less expensive for the nurse and provides the opportunity to use equipment that cannot be taken to the home.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In a two-way referral system, who fills out the second half of the referral form?
questions.rationale: The receiving agency records services done, findings and recommendations and sends it back via the family.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Two-way referral (PDF p. 90)
questions.quote: The personnel ofthe agency to which referral is made fills up the second hatfof the form

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The nurse and a hypertensive client sign an agreement listing steps to reduce salt intake, with agreed rewards for each step achieved. This intervention is:
questions.rationale: Contracting uses a written agreement and positive reinforcement to achieve complex behavior change.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Contracting (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Contracting provides a systematic method of increasing desirable client behavior through the use of the principle of positive reinforcement.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: To eliminate breeding sites of Aedes mosquitoes at home, the nurse teaches the family to:
options: Change water in vases at least every 2 days
Leave old tires to collect rain
questions.rationale: Aedes aegypti breeds in clean stagnant water in artificial containers; change water and remove containers.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 3 Home environment (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: change water in flower vases at least every two days or not to allow water to remain stagnant in artificial containers

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: For small group health discussions with families sharing the same problem, the ideal group size is about:
questions.rationale: A group of 8 is ideal, with a maximum of 15.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 4 Competency-based teaching (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: For this technique to be effective a group of 8 is ideal with a maximum of 15.
